body:
Part of #380. Four commits, each gated on the full suite plus the free-start sweep.

## Baselines and final state

Baseline at dev 8484ea5: FreeStartSweepBench 104/104 at 56.0-57.1 s (6 runs over 2 s: j716 both, j347 both, j335 shift, j346 base), `:core:check -PslowTests` green at ~3m10s. Final state at the branch tip: **104/104 at 56.8 s, same 6 over-2s captures, slowTests green at 3m16s**. Nothing regresses; gh283-j925-farseed (7.2 s) and gh283-j990-cold (0.6 s) keep their FAST 20 s budgets, loopmm-tight-t39-fast lands at 18.9 s of its 90 s budget.

## Commit 1: ALM+snap removal (ruling)

Deletes SnapRepairPolish, AlmBfgsCore, SmoothJumpProblem, FacingReconstruction, AlmSnapStage and their five dedicated tests, plus the razor-era probes that only drove them (RazorBench, MiqcpClose, ProofNeighborhoodProbe; nothing else referenced them). RunMatrixScreen loses the `alm<sec>` sweep arm; RunMatrixSweepTest keeps parse coverage that the base is now rejected; TESTS.md updated. -7,358 lines.

Method audit on what the cluster held alive:
- `TranslationEliminationTest` splits: its brute-force tests pin live Scoring/WrapWindowIls behavior (`PathTranslation.bestTranslation` is production code) and stay, with `translatedEvaluate`/`translatedSlack` as their oracle; the two ALM-era transCoef tests die with SmoothJumpProblem.
- `JumpLinearModel.boostAt/forwardMag/strafeMag` stay: contrary to the issue premise, MiqcpDump and StructureVariantDump still feed the live tools/miqcp pipeline (used by the recent roc2 cell-set MILP work).
- `Angles.travelDeg` stays with SmoothLambdaScoringTest.
- `PathTranslation.clampAxis`/`ulpShift` lose their last users and go.

## Commit 2 (target 5): audit-dead ladder rungs

Temporary rung-win instrumentation over both corpora (sweep 104 runs + ProblemsTest 111 problems):
- `recoverStart`'s margin ladder beyond the first margin: ~30k runs, **0 wins** anywhere; collapsed to the first-margin translation (the certify-else-fallback always returned that same point).
- The relaxation seed grid's plain/projection rung: **0 of 70** full 160/220-call SLP solves ever landed; dropped.
- Everything else contributes and stays: CF margins m0-m7 and both robust ladders, all 4 inertia passes, the window CF/SLP alternates (36 and 15 window wins), the free-joint rungs (win via recovered starts), chain alternates, LevelSetAscent (44 wins).

## Commit 3 (target 4): wrap-close re-accumulation scoring

`WrapWindowIls` gains opt-in `reaccumScore` (evaluate through `wrapAll` + `toGameFacings`); `jointWrapClose` uses it and picks the final translation from the same re-accumulated chain. The close's ILS zero now equals the acceptance violation exactly (j716: both 7.77e-6, previously ils 3.3e-6 vs reaccum 4.6e-5), so a close reaching zero certifies immediately; farseed's close now certifies at a true zero. Raw scoring stays the default for WrapIlsNode and the WrapWindowIlsTest pins. j716 stays budget-bound: its honest re-accumulated floor is nonzero.

## Commit 4 (target 6): staged race replaced by a sequential explore stage

Traced across the corpus, the race's parallel overlap never happens: every FAST primary either lands (no explore) or starves in seconds (loopmm-fast 4.2 s, dfneo 0.03 s) and explore spawns via the primary-done-infeasible branch, which is already sequential; the 20 s checkpoint never fires post-momentum-removal. The two threads, polling loop, checkpoint, and cross-cancellation collapse into primary-then-explore inline with the same arbitration and run-record race info. loopmm-tight-t39-fast: 18.9 s vs 19.1 s, identical objective.

## Measured skips

- **Target 2 (eval-loop allocation, compile caching)**: JFR over the sweep: `JumpConstraintCompiler.compile` 0 of 5,077 CPU samples, `toGameFacings` 0.4%, total GC pause 0.15 s of 56 s. The ForwardPath allocation (19% of alloc samples, effectively free) sits inside the ExactJumpModel no-go zone. Bounded under ~1% of wall; skipped.
- **Target 3 (free-start translation unification)**: farseed's 7.3 s measures as ~3.6 s of pattern-round theta scans plus ~3.2 s wrap-close descent; translation implementations are not in the profile. Unifying the analytic O(m) `bestTranslate`/`pinTranslate` onto the 60-iteration ternary `PathTranslation` (whose `axisF` is already 10% of sweep CPU) would add cost and shift knife-edge semantics for no measured gain. recoverStart's loop, the one measured redundancy, went in commit 2.
- **Target 1 (SLP/simplex)**: implemented a shifted-nonnegative reformulation (box lower bounds and the unrestricted-variable column eliminated, phase-2 slack variable substituted away). Sweep: **56.6 s -> 38.0 s (-33%), 104/104, over-2s 6 -> 4**. The slow gate rejected it: dualrecovery/j346 chain-stuck, loopmm-3jump-lands hug 5e-4 short, both loopmm-tight-t39 rescues lost their landing. Same LP, different optimal vertices; the pinned chains depend on commons-math's incidental vertex selection. Reverted. Any future SLP replacement (bespoke bounded solver included) faces the same sensitivity and needs either vertex reproduction or a ruling re-pinning those gates; the measured -33% says it is worth its own issue.

## Open ruling (deferred, not decided)

RelaxationRecovery's post-seed tail (the LatticeRepair branch and the pin-widths phase) won **0 of 38** attempts across both corpora while costing ~13.6 s of corpus wall time. It was not removed because `rrPinWidths` and the `lr*` params on the dualChain node belong to the graph editor param surface ruled kept in #380. Removing tail + params, keeping both, or removing the tail while retiring its params needs a call.
title: feat(solver): remove the ALM+snap research and run the ranked simplification review
